meta_description: Chain-of-custody evidence is becoming a market-access requirement, not a marketing story.

blocks.x: Chain-of-custody evidence is becoming a market-access requirement, not a marketing story.

The argument for EUDR made provenance a compliance deadline is simple: decisions made on stale information cost more than the platform that would make them current — and the gap is measurable in weeks, not years.

items: Capture at source (mobile-first for farmers) decides data quality more than ledger choice.
Role-based verification: regulators, buyers and auditors each see only what their role permits.
Verified provenance is premium positioning: the market pays for proof.

blocks.x: Three questions to ask your current vendors

items: Ask for the baseline: how was the starting position measured, and who signed it?
Ask for the trail: can your auditors replay any decision the system made last week, end to end?
Ask for the unit cost: what does one decision cost to run, and who owns keeping it down?

blocks.x: Programs like EUDR made provenance a compliance deadline rarely fail on the technology. They fail on unnamed ownership, unmeasured baselines and ungated scope — the three failure modes the guards on this page are built for.

items: Every stage has a gate with real stop authority — scope expands on measured deltas, not on momentum.
The operating model is designed first — who decides what, at which gate, holding which evidence.
Evidence is generated while the work happens, so the audit is a walkthrough, not an archaeology project.

blocks.x: Regulator queries that took weeks of document hunts now resolve in hours with anchored evidence.
Where this shows up in our work

This perspective is grounded in Blockchain Analytics & Regulatory Compliance and Enterprise DLT Network Engineering within the Blockchain & Digital Trust tower — each carried by our platforms with governance and evidence built in.
If the argument lands, the next step is small: a working session with the practice lead to test it against your estate.
